name: fold-stale-edit-of-a-lower-case-name-is-denied-through-an-upper-case-class-where-the-disk-folds-case
description: tracked.yaml lists docs/*.md and strict_mode.yaml docs/[A-Z]*.md; the disk holds docs/plan.md. Session A reads docs/plan.md, session B reads it, edits it and commits, so A's read is stale; A then pre-edits docs/plan.md, the disk's own spelling. As written, the class [A-Z] does not accept p. On a case-insensitive disk (caseless) docs/plan.md also opens as docs/Plan.md, which the class does accept, so the folded name meets the class folded with it (it accepts p as it accepts P) and A is denied exactly as strict_mode 05 denies a stale edit, with the reason and summary.path echoing docs/plan.md as A sent it. Where the disk keeps case apart (nfd, none) no spelling of docs/plan.md is strict: the pre-edit falls through to warn mode and is allowed with the collision warning against B's grant and the disk-differs notice of warn_mode 36, both naming docs/plan.md. Fold 14 is the control: docs/Plan.md is denied on every disk. The two summary timestamps are ignored; every other summary field is compared. Both backends.
